title: 领导力 Day 13：授权与放手 — 从微管理到信任的档位
title_en: Leadership Day 13: Delegation — From Micromanaging to Trust Levels

questions.question: 同一个设计 API 契约的任务要交给一个新人和一个资深工程师，按「信任阶梯」该怎么做？
options: 为了公平起见，对两人统一用第 4 档共定，避免让任何一方觉得被区别对待
按「人×任务」给不同档位，并把「这件事我在第几档」说出口
对新人全程盯紧每个 endpoint，对资深则只在上线前做一次最终审批
对两人都先给第 7 档全权以示信任，出了问题再把决定权收回
questions.explanation: 文章说授权档位是「人 × 任务」的函数，不是你的固定性格：新人在第 7 档会淹死，资深在第 1 档会窒息。关键一句是把档位讲出口，避免「我以为你会先问我」。对新人全程盯每个细节实际是第 1 档，文章示范给新人的是第 4 档。
questions.question_en: The same task — designing a new service's API contract — goes to a new hire and a senior engineer. What does the Trust Ladder say to do?
options_en: For fairness, put both at level 4 (decide together) so neither feels treated differently
Set different levels by person × task — e.g., co-decide with the new hire, full authority for the senior — and say aloud which level you're at
Watch every endpoint the new hire writes, and give the senior one final approval before launch
Give both full authority at level 7 to show trust, and take decisions back if something goes wrong
questions.explanation_en: The piece says delegation level is a function of person × task, not your fixed personality: a newcomer at level 7 drowns, a senior at level 1 suffocates. The key move is to name the level out loud to avoid "I thought you'd check with me first." Watching every detail is effectively level 1; the piece's example puts the new hire at level 4.

questions.question: 你 review 下属的实现：方案能跑、完全可逆，只是不是你会选的写法。文章建议怎么处理？
options: 直接在 PR 里改成更优的写法并附上原因，让他通过对比学习
要求他按你的方案重写，因为 80% 的解法在长期会积累技术债
不接管，说明这是风格不是对错、由他来定，约好两周后看监控数据
当下先放行，但把这次记录下来，留到绩效评估时一并反馈
questions.explanation: 先问「这可逆吗？三周后改回来贵吗」——不贵就放手。接管会让他学到「反正老板最后会改成他的样子」，下次干脆不动脑。文章明说 80% 的解法加他的成长，常常胜过 100% 的解法加他的依赖；留到绩效时清算则是会杀死授权文化的秋后算账。
questions.question_en: Reviewing a report's implementation, you find it works and is fully reversible — just not how you'd write it. What does the piece recommend?
options_en: Rewrite it in the PR the better way with your reasons, so they learn by comparison
Have them redo it your way, since an 80% solution piles up tech debt over time
Don't take over; say it's style not correctness, let them decide, and agree to check the monitoring in two weeks
Let it through for now but note it down to raise at performance review time
questions.explanation_en: First ask whether it's reversible and whether undoing it in three weeks would be costly — if not, let go. Taking over teaches them the boss will rewrite it anyway, so they stop thinking. The piece says an 80% solution plus their growth often beats a 100% solution plus their dependence; saving it for the review is the after-the-fact reckoning that kills delegation culture.

questions.question: 关于「把猴子还回去」的教练式提问，文章认为在什么情况下反而应该直接告诉答案？
options: 对方是资深工程师，只是想让你为他的决定背书的时候
问题涉及架构选型这类影响较大的技术决策的时候
任务紧急、涉及安全，或者对方确实没有相关背景的时候
你确信自己的答案明显比对方能想到的更好的时候
questions.explanation: 文章的边界条款：火烧眉毛、涉及安全，或新人没方向时一直反问，那是折磨不是 coaching。资深的人只想要背书，恰恰是该把决定还给他的情形；而「我的答案更好」正是「建议怪兽」的 IC 惯性，架构选型本身就是文中示范要反问的例子。
questions.question_en: On giving the monkey back through coaching questions, when does the piece say you should simply tell them the answer instead?
options_en: When they're a senior engineer who just wants you to endorse their decision
When the question is a high-impact technical decision like an architecture choice
When the task is urgent, involves safety, or the person genuinely lacks the background
When you're confident your answer is clearly better than what they'd come up with
questions.explanation_en: The piece's boundary: when things are on fire, safety is involved, or a newcomer has no bearings, endless counter-questions are torture, not coaching. A senior who just wants your blessing is exactly when to hand the decision back; "my answer is better" is the advice-monster IC habit; and an architecture choice is the very example the piece uses for asking first.
